title: Use home-zone instants for calendar cache and CalDAV query windows
description:
## Finding

Calendar APIs accept local calendar dates and resolve events in the configured home zone, but cache and CalDAV range boundaries reinterpret those dates as UTC midnight. This drops valid events at one edge of the requested local day and uses a fixed 24-hour end step across DST.

`load_cached` converts `from` and `to` with `day_ms`, whose implementation explicitly constructs midnight UTC. It then adds `86_400_000` for the inclusive final day. For a western home zone the UTC end is earlier than local end, so evening events on the final local day can be omitted. For an eastern home zone the UTC start is later than local start, so early events on the first local day can be omitted. On 23- or 25-hour DST days the fixed millisecond addition is also the wrong next local midnight.

The CalDAV full-fetch filter repeats the mismatch by formatting both local `NaiveDate` bounds directly with a literal `Z`, so the remote server may omit those edge events before they ever enter the cache. Stored event instants and recurrence expansion otherwise use resolved zones, making the query layer internally inconsistent.

## Evidence at audited commit

* `crates/thegn-host/src/hydrate_calendar.rs:288-295`: cache reads call `day_ms(from)` and `day_ms(to) + 86_400_000`.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/hydrate_calendar.rs:384-388`: `day_ms` defines a local date as midnight UTC.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/db_calendar.rs:55-91`: overlap filtering trusts those instant bounds.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/calendar/caldav.rs:70-86`: `calendar-query` appends `Z` without resolving the home zone.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/hydrate_calendar.rs:55-82`: the caller explicitly derives the requested horizon/month in `home_zone`.

## Impact

Users outside UTC can silently lose meetings from month/agenda views and reminder candidate loading. The exact missing edge changes by UTC offset and DST transition, making the defect intermittent and difficult to diagnose. A full CalDAV replacement can persist the omission until a later horizon fetch.

## Required implementation

* Define date windows as `[start of from in home zone, start of day after to in home zone)`.
* Resolve both boundaries through the calendar's explicit gap/ambiguity policy, then convert the resulting instants to UTC milliseconds.
* Never derive the next local day by adding 86,400,000 milliseconds.
* Pass resolved UTC instants—not naïve dates mislabeled with `Z`—to CalDAV time-range construction. Make the end-exclusive semantics explicit.
* Keep all-day event semantics and recurrence masters correct, and make cache horizon metadata use the same canonical range type.
* Centralize this conversion so local cache, remote filtering, reminder scanning, and tests cannot drift.

## Verification

Test positive and negative UTC offsets, half-hour/quarter-hour zones, spring-forward and fall-back dates, events exactly at both boundaries, all-day events, midnight-exclusive endings, and CalDAV request XML. Prove cache and provider windows select the same instant interval.

## Dependencies

Dependency-ready. The typed page/cursor work in <issue id="0983c521-7456-4ce7-b924-6ef073009447" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-452/separate-calendar-page-mode-from-the-returned-sync-cursor">THE-452</issue> and atomic cache work in <issue id="03224068-8a1f-413d-87fb-65b45fd6c833" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-451/commit-calendar-pages-tombstones-and-sync-cursors-atomically">THE-451</issue> must consume this canonical range representation rather than reintroducing naïve boundaries.
